claims.text: Integrating density functional theory with phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately predict high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach is applicable to identifying high-entropy alloys for thermal-insulation applications.
An alloy's microstructure and chemical composition mediate its phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics.
Ab initio calculations or molecular-dynamics simulations can predict phonon scattering and thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will improve prediction accuracy relative to current prediction methods for high-entropy alloys.
Computational-resource limitations constrain the applicability of the proposed approach.
Complex alloy compositions constrain the applicability of the proposed approach.
Experimental validation is needed to establish the accuracy of the predicted properties.
DFT prediction accuracy is uncertain for complex multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-flash analysis can be used to measure phonon thermal conductivity for the proposed benchmark.
The benchmark will compare predicted and experimentally measured phonon thermal conductivity across a set of high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if prediction errors exceed 10% for a majority of the tested alloys.
